items.prompt: A disc robot's centre follows the straight path segment from (0, 0) to (4, 0) m. An obstacle, already inflated by the robot's radius, is a circle centred at (2, 1.5) m with radius 0.5 m. Find the minimum distance in metres from the obstacle centre to any point of the path segment. Give the distance to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m).
items.solution: d = (4, 0), w = (2, 1.5), t = (w·d)/(d·d) = 0.5; t is inside [0, 1], so the closest point is interior (2, 0). Distance = 1.5 m, greater than the inflated radius 0.5 m, so the path is clear.
hints: Drop a perpendicular from the obstacle centre onto the path and check whether its foot lies between the two endpoints.
With d = end - start = (4, 0) and w = centre - start = (2, 1.5), compute t = (w·d)/(d·d), clamp it to [0, 1], and find the closest point start + t·d; then measure to the centre.
d = (4, 0), w = (2, 1.5), t = (w·d)/(d·d) = 0.5; t is inside [0, 1], so the closest point is interior (2, 0). Distance = 1.5 m, greater than the inflated radius 0.5 m, so the path is clear.
items.remediation: If you answered 2.5 you only measured to the endpoints; here the closest point is in the middle of the path. Revisit /lessons/R03.

items.prompt: A disc robot's centre follows the straight path segment from (0, 0) to (4, 0) m. An obstacle, already inflated by the robot's radius, is a circle centred at (6, 1) m with radius 0.5 m. Find the minimum distance in metres from the obstacle centre to any point of the path segment. Give the distance to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m).
items.solution: d = (4, 0), w = (6, 1), t = (w·d)/(d·d) = 1.5; t is above 1, so clamp it to 1: the closest point is the end (4, 0). Distance = 2.236068 m, greater than the inflated radius 0.5 m, so the path is clear. The infinite-line distance would be 1 m, which is not the segment distance.

items.prompt: A disc robot's centre follows the straight path segment from (1, 1) to (5, 4) m. An obstacle, already inflated by the robot's radius, is a circle centred at (-2, 2) m with radius 1 m. Find the minimum distance in metres from the obstacle centre to any point of the path segment. Give the distance to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m).
items.solution: d = (4, 3), w = (-3, 1), t = (w·d)/(d·d) = -0.36; t is below 0, so clamp it to 0: the closest point is the start (1, 1). Distance = 3.162278 m, greater than the inflated radius 1 m, so the path is clear. The infinite-line distance would be 2.6 m, which is not the segment distance.

items.prompt: A tool centre moves along the straight segment from (1, 1) to (1, 1) m. An obstacle, already inflated by the tool radius, is a circle centred at (4, 5) m with radius 1 m. Find the minimum distance in metres from the obstacle centre to any point of the tool's segment. This is a geometry check, not a hardware clearance authorization. Give the distance to at least 3 decimal places (graded within ±0.001 m).
items.solution: The segment has zero length, so it is the point (1, 1). Distance = sqrt(3² + 4²) = 5 m, greater than the inflated radius 1 m, so the path is clear.
hints: The start and end points coincide, so the 'segment' is a single point; the projection formula would divide by zero.
Treat the segment as the single point (1, 1); next compute the ordinary distance from (4, 5) to it.
The segment has zero length, so it is the point (1, 1). Distance = sqrt(3² + 4²) = 5 m, greater than the inflated radius 1 m, so the path is clear.
items.remediation: If your calculation failed or returned NaN, you divided by the zero segment length; a zero-length segment is just its point. Revisit /lessons/R03.
